name: maths
title: More mathematics and formal methods
summary: SageMath and Macaulay2 for mathematics beyond the base pack; the Coq proof assistant; the Spin and TLA+ model checkers; CBMC for C programs. Lean and Isabelle are in their own packs.

tools.name: sagemath
tools.does: a large mathematics system: number theory, algebra, combinatorics, geometry and symbolic calculus (through its built-in Maxima), with its own Python-like language. Takes a second or two to start

tools.name: macaulay2
tools.does: commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: ideals, modules, resolutions, sheaf cohomology
tools.check: printf 'R = QQ[x,y,z]; I = ideal(x^2-y*z, y^2-x*z); print degree I\n' > t.m2; M2 --script t.m2

tools.name: coq
tools.does: the Coq proof assistant (now called Rocq): checks proofs written in its language
tools.check:
printf 'Theorem t : forall n:nat, n + 0 = n.
Proof. induction n; simpl; [reflexivity | rewrite IHn; reflexivity]. Qed.
Print Assumptions t.
' > t.v; coqc t.v

tools.name: spin
tools.does: model checker for concurrent systems described in Promela

tools.name: tla+
tools.does: the TLA+ tools: the TLC model checker for specifications of concurrent and distributed systems
tools.check:
cat > T.tla <<'EOF'
---- MODULE T ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLE x
Init == x = 0
Next == (x < 3 /\ x' = x + 1) \/ (x = 3 /\ x' = x)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_x
Inv == x <= 3
====
EOF
printf 'SPECIFICATION Spec\nINVARIANT Inv\n' > T.cfg; java -cp /opt/tla2tools.jar tlc2.TLC -metadir /tmp/tlc T.tla 2>&1 | grep -c 'No error has been found'

tools.name: cbmc
tools.does: bounded model checker for C programs: proves assertions, or finds an input that breaks them, up to a bound on loops
tools.usage: cbmc FILE.c --unwind N   (assertions with __CPROVER_assert, assumptions with __CPROVER_assume)
tools.check: printf 'int main(){int x; __CPROVER_assume(x>0 && x<10); __CPROVER_assert(x*x<100,"square"); return 0;}\n' > t.c; cbmc t.c 2>&1 | tail -1
